originalRequest: Produce the English variant of the shipped Chinese course learn-context-engineering for learn.agentmentor.dev. Teaching rewrite in English (not a translation): same 6-lesson structure, same lesson slugs, same interactive-block ids and answer positions, source quotes restored to their verbatim English originals from sources.md, runnable code kept logic-identical with only comments and user-facing strings translated, cross-course references pointing at the live English course titles, natural desk-voice English prose with no AI-slop register.

briefCompleteness.evidence: The owner ratified the multilingual plan explicitly: all six locales on learn.agentmentor.dev, English first, batches of 2-3 courses in path order with a commit per course. The zh course is the verified source of truth for scope, learner model, structure, and grounding, so no additional clarification was needed.

learnerModel.targetReader: A developer who has finished the first seven courses in this series, can hand-write a stop_reason-driven loop, and wants to control what the model sees on every turn of a long task
knownConcepts: The messages history growing every turn; tool_result blocks returning together
The context window as a finite resource (course 5)
Subagents starting from an independent context and returning only conclusions (course 6)
Basic JavaScript / Node.js reading and writing
unknownConcepts: Context engineering as the progression of prompt engineering
The attention budget and context rot as an economics of tokens
System-prompt altitude (brittle hardcoding vs vague guidance vs strong heuristics)
Tools and examples as context; canonical examples over edge-case laundry lists
Preload vs just-in-time retrieval; lightweight identifiers and progressive disclosure
Compaction strategy: what must survive, what can go
Subagents as a context-management technique and their token economics
learnerModel.assumedEnvironment: A Node.js environment, terminal access, and a text editor; the course 7 harness code available to extend
learnerModel.firstIndependentAction: Take one of their own long agent sessions and mark which context entered by preload versus retrieval, and what should have been compacted
noviceRamp: Lesson 1 grounds the discipline in the attention budget and context rot before any technique
Lesson 2 dissects what already counts as context (system prompt altitude, tools, examples)
Lesson 3 draws the preload vs just-in-time boundary with lightweight identifiers
Lesson 4 adds compaction and structured notes for long tasks
Lesson 5 reframes subagents through context economics, and lesson 6 wires tracking + threshold compaction + NOTES.md onto the course-7 harness

learnerBrief: The target reader has finished the first seven courses, can hand-write the harness loop, and reads JavaScript. They don't yet know how to govern what enters the window each turn. The course gets them to explain context engineering via the attention budget and context rot, fix system-prompt altitude, split preload from just-in-time retrieval, design compaction and structured notes for long tasks, reason about subagents in token economics, and finally wire token tracking, threshold-triggered compaction, and a NOTES.md notebook onto the course-7 harness.
scope: Covered: context engineering vs prompt engineering, attention budget and context rot, system-prompt altitude, tools and examples as context, preload vs just-in-time retrieval with lightweight identifiers and progressive disclosure, compaction strategy and structured note-taking, subagents as context isolation with their token economics, and a hands-on context-management layer on the course-7 harness. Not covered: prompt-writing technique (course 3), cross-session persistence and recovery (course 5), multi-agent collaboration patterns beyond the context lens (course 6), and RAG or vector databases. Depth: from zero to running a task too big for one window through a self-managed context layer.

qualitySelfReview.diagramUse: Diagrams are kept exactly where the zh original uses them (the context-anatomy layout and the compaction flow), with labels rewritten in English; none added or removed. What-enters-the-window-each-turn is spatial content a diagram carries well, and the zh placement was already review-validated.
weakestPoints: S5 (the community roadmap) contains the opinionated 'prompt engineering is dead' line; the course quotes it only as that source's stance and leads with S1's 'natural progression' framing — readers skimming may still overweight the slogan
Token figures (4x/15x, 1,000-2,000-token summaries) are Anthropic's reported data for specific systems, framed as such rather than as constants
Lesson 6's compaction implementation is teaching-grade; production systems should prefer native compaction APIs where available, which the lesson states

As an English teaching rewrite of a verified zh course, idiomatic drift is the residual risk: source quotes were restored verbatim from English originals and runnable code kept logic-identical, but prose was re-taught rather than translated, so review must check meaning-equivalence against the zh lessons

acceptanceReview.terminalTask: The learner can take a long task that exceeds one context window, split its context into preload and just-in-time retrieval, wire token-usage tracking with threshold-triggered compaction and a NOTES.md notebook onto a stop_reason-driven harness, and run the task to completion while explaining what each compaction kept and why.
acceptanceReview.interactionCheck: Six agentmentor-check blocks, one per lesson (finite attention in L1, altitude fix in L2, strategy trade-off in L3, compaction trade-off in L4, clean window in L5, notes-every-turn in L6), preserved from the zh variant with identical ids, modes, choice counts, and correct-answer positions; label, prompt, whyHere, choice text, and feedback are English teaching rewrites specific to each lesson's misconception. Exercises keep the zh Level structure with rubric, answer, and hints per Level.
acceptanceReview.learnerFitCheck: The course assumes the prior seven courses: the harness loop, the finite window, and subagent basics. The attention-budget economics, altitude, retrieval boundary, compaction, and isolation are taught from zero in dependency order; the learner first builds the full context layer in lesson 6, after every prerequisite. Lesson 1's first exercise asks only for an audit of the reader's own session.
